title: The source index of a movement op
hints: Expand(shape) carries the shape of the source. Which of the source's axes have only one element, and what is the only index you can ask there?
Walk two lists together with zip. For expand, pair each size in shape with the index entry on the same axis.
Expand returns [0 if s == 1 else i for s, i in zip(shape, idx)]. Shrink returns [i + o for i, o in zip(idx, offsets)].
prompt: src(op, idx) answers one question: when a movement op is asked for its element at index idx, which index does it ask its source for? The Permute case is written. Fix the other two, which pass the index on unchanged. Expand(shape) carries the shape of the source, the value being expanded, so you can see which axes have size 1. Shrink(offsets) carries one offset per axis.

answer.explain: A movement op never touches a value. It only says which index of its source to ask. Permute reorders the index, expand asks every size-1 axis at 0 because that is the only element the source has there, and shrink adds the offset of each axis. The output index goes in and the source index comes out, with no loads and no arithmetic on data.
